item: A custody entry the ingest could not write is queued with the hash and columns the ingest read, so the late entry binds the stored bytes
summary: _maybe_record_custody read the article's hash and metadata before touching the log but queued the id alone (note_failed(article_id, error=...)), so the drain read the row's CURRENT hash: an in-place Article.hash rewrite between a failed write and the drain bound the late entry to bytes the ingest never stored. The columns the ingest read (item_hash, url, canonical_url, source_id) now ride the queued record; when the read itself is the failure the queue carries the id alone and the drain reads the row, as before. Passing the hash alone would have dropped url/canonical_url/source_id from the late entry (the drain reads the row only when item_hash is absent), so all four are queued. Three tests, two red on the unchanged pipeline; hash-only and no-columns mutants both red. Relies on WAL #1623's drain for the hash check; the queue shape is the same on main.
